title: capacity-leasebook-and-throttle-harmonizer-for-stable-dedicated-throughput
author: Maya Chen
description: Context: Dedicated customers observed P95 latency spikes during short high-frequency bursts that consumed warm-pool headroom and caused aggressive preemption of committed capacity; this PR introduces a Capacity Leasebook and a Throttle Harmonizer to smooth those microbursts and preserve long-running throughput guarantees. Motivation: decouple short-lived burst reservations from sustained commitments so that priority tenants see consistent throughput while still allowing opportunistic short bursts. High-level changes: new leasebook controller that issues timeboxed 'leases' for burst capacity; soft-lease arbitration algorithm (probabilistic decay + runway smoothing) to avoid synchronized drain; harmonizer in scheduler that computes gentle per-tenant throttles when short-lease utilization exceeds configured runway thresholds; telemetry for per-lease lifespan histograms, preemption counts, effective throughput by commit window, and headroom pressure signals. Rollout plan: feature-flagged (config.redwood.enableLeasebook=false by default), opt-in migration tool for existing reservations, canary on 10% of Dedicated clusters, full rollout after 2 weeks if no regressions. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked (internal) and linear tickets referenced; - [x] unit tests for lease allocator and harmonizer; - [x] deterministic integration test for preemption/backoff scenarios; - [x] load tests showing P50/P95 SLO improvement for committed tenants; - [x] console metrics and dashboards updated; - [ ] staged rollout recipe applied to production fleets. Commits summary: 1) Add leasebook controller, CRD, and api types (6 files) 2) Implement soft-lease allocator and decay policy with tunables (3 files) 3) Integrate harmonizer with scheduler decision path + tests (4 files) 4) Add telemetry hooks, dashboards, and migration script (3 files) 5) Docs, changelog, and rollout notes (2 files). Changed areas (high level): pkg/controller/leasebook/*, pkg/scheduler/harmonizer.go, pkg/scheduler/decision.go (throttle hooks), pkg/telemetry/lease_metrics.go, deploy/helm/values.dedicated.yaml (feature flag), tools/migrate-reservations.sh, docs/dedicated/leasebook.md. Test plan and CI: initial CI run flagged a flaky util test (util/alloc_test) at first; reran unit and integration suites; all checks green on second run; e2e burst load validated on a 4-node Dedicated canary (results attached in PR CI artifacts). Review conversation summary: "Rohit Singh: please bound per-lease memory to avoid unbounded metadata growth;" -> "Author: added a bounded ring for short-lived leases and unit test exercising high churn;" "Lena Ortiz: add tenant and reservation tags to metrics for easier pivoting in console;" -> "Author: added tenant_id and reservation_type labels and updated dashboards;" "Ben Carter: can you provide a canary rollout recipe and rollback plan?" -> "Author: included canary recipe and automatic-disable hook, plus migration script that is idempotent;" Approvals: Rohit and Lena approved after requested changes implemented; Ben approved after canary notes. CI status: pass (lint/unit/integration/e2e). Merge: squash-and-merge by Maya Chen after approvals and green CI; merge commit: abcdef1. Notes: This PR intentionally keeps the default flag off to avoid surprise behavior for existing Dedicated customers; telemetry keys are versioned so downstream alerts won't break on rollout.
